lines: Wiz co-founder and CTO Ami Luttwak argues that 'Black October', a wave of AI-found vulnerabilities, marks a turning point: AI now lets attackers find and exploit flaws at machine speed, making human-paced patching cycles largely obsolete.
He says the exploitation window has collapsed from months to roughly 20 minutes, and fast-improving open-source models have erased the buffer between a frontier model's release and its weaponization.

His prescription is continuous self-attack with 'red agent' swarms built on the latest models, plus secure-by-design architectures that assume zero-days exist and rely on isolation and process lockdown.

Luttwak contends much of today's security work, such as compliance reporting and static configuration checks, adds little protection, and that unauthenticated internet-facing exposure like hard-coded keys in mobile apps is the more urgent risk.

To contain AI costs he recommends tiered pipelines where deterministic checks and cheap models filter events before costly models verify, and he expects a 'new 90s' era forcing a reboot of vendor stacks toward AI-native tools.
title: Every Day Is Zero Day | Wiz CTO Ami Luttwak
